title: Design a Data Labeling Platform
prompt: Design a platform that distributes labeling tasks (e.g. image annotation, RLHF preference comparisons) to a large pool of human labelers, collects their responses, and produces a quality-controlled labeled dataset for model training.
requirements: Functional: assign tasks to available labelers, collect and store responses, support multiple labelers per task for quality/agreement checks, export a finished labeled dataset
Non-functional: tens of thousands of labelers working concurrently, tasks should not be assigned to the same labeler twice, low-quality labelers should be identifiable
discussion_points: Task assignment/queueing so labelers aren't idle and tasks aren't double-assigned under concurrency
Quality control: redundant labeling, agreement scoring, and flagging or downweighting unreliable labelers
Data model for tasks, assignments, responses, and the final aggregated label
Handling labelers who abandon a task mid-way (timeouts, reassignment)
Scaling task throughput as both the labeler pool and task volume grow
How the platform would support a fundamentally different task type (e.g. free-text RLHF ranking vs. bounding boxes) without a rewrite
